_about: Customer words for every message the server sends to a screen (UI standard, product owner 2026-10-16): a short label for the main screen and a structured detail — what it means, why, what to do next — for its pop-up. Read by core/messages.py; values fill {placeholders}.

detail.what: The request could not be completed.
detail.next: Try again. If it keeps happening, raise a request in Support and say when it happened.

detail.what: What you asked for does not exist, or your organisation cannot see it.
Your role does not include this action.
detail.next: Ask an administrator in your organisation.

detail.what: {what}
The asset has no coordinates, so no hazard can be read at it.
detail.next: Add the asset's latitude and longitude in Your data.

detail.what: The {map} have not been read at this location yet.
detail.next: Run losses again — a run reads any new location first.

detail.what: The location lies outside the area the {map} cover.
Your organisation has not chosen the damage curves for {peril} losses.
The damage curves chosen for {peril} do not yet match the hazard data the platform holds.
detail.next: Choose another family of curves in Settings → Methodology, or wait for the platform to support these.

detail.what: The building's use (residential, commercial or industrial) is not stated, and the asset type '{type}' does not settle it.
detail.next: State the building use in Your data.

detail.what: Neither the building's use nor the asset's type is stated.
detail.next: State the building use in Your data.

detail.what: The asset's country is not stated, and damage curves are chosen by country.{hint}
detail.next: State the country in Your data.

loss.gap.country_group.label: Country is a group, not a country

detail.what: Your data states '{stated}', a group of countries; damage curves are chosen by country.{hint}
detail.next: State the asset's own country in Your data.

loss.gap.no_curve.label: No curve for this use and country

detail.what: The chosen damage curves include no {use} curve for {country}.
detail.why: The publisher did not publish one for this region.

detail.what: The building's own value (land excluded) is not stated.
detail.why: A damage curve gives a share of the building's value; a market or appraised value includes the land, so it is never used instead.
detail.next: Add the building value in Your data.

detail.what: A holding is a share in a company, not a building, so no building damage curve applies to it.
The site's building value is not stated; its annual value is a flow, not what the building is worth.
detail.next: Add the building value in Your data.

detail.what: The asset's value is not stated.

loss.gap.no_damage_range.label: No damage range at this depth

detail.what: The damage curve publishes no range at a depth of {depth} m.
No published projection of {peril} is available yet, so only today's figure exists.
The flood projections the platform uses were not run for {scenario}.
detail.why: The publisher ran two warming pathways only.

detail.what: The flood projections the platform uses publish no map for {year}; their last period, 2060–2099, is offered as 2080.
Local flood defences here are designed for the 1-in-{years}-year river flood. Losses from more frequent floods are set to zero.
detail.why: Source: the JRC map of estimated flood-protection standards in Europe.

detail.what: The flood-protection map has not been read at this location yet; the loss shown is undefended.
detail.next: Run losses again — a run reads any new location first.

detail.what: The flood-protection map holds no value at this location; the loss shown is undefended.
The location lies outside the flood-protection map (geographical Europe except Russia, Belarus, Ukraine and the Caucasus); the loss shown is undefended.
Defences are not applied to future climates yet.
detail.why: The projections' publisher moves protection levels with the climate, using its own protection data — a method not yet decided.

detail.what: The map's publisher flags this area: depths above 10 m in small channels may come from the model or the terrain data rather than a real flood.
